mainTopic: Using worshipped things for the בית המקדש: attached items, the קל וחומר debate, and change in form
overview: The גמרא asks whether a נעבד במחובר, an item attached to the ground that was worshipped, is forbidden for the בית המקדש even though an ordinary person may use it. A follow-up question asks whether this also covers מכשירי קרבן, such as the מזבח. רבא answers with a קל וחומר from אתנן: a prostitute's payment is forbidden for the Temple even when attached, so a worshipped item should be too. רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע flips the argument to reach the opposite, lenient result, and shows that the phrase 'בית ה׳ אלהיך' is already used for another teaching. רבא replies that when a קל וחומר can go either way, we choose the strict direction. רב פפא challenges this rule from רבי עקיבא's lenient reasoning about הזאה for the פסח. The גמרא answers that רבי עקיבא was only reminding רבי אליעזר of a tradition he had learned from him. Then רמי בר חמא asks a new question: does a change in form, such as wheat ground into flour, remove the ban of a נעבד for מנחות? מר זוטרא tries to answer from the dispute about offspring of animals forbidden for the מזבח, and the גמרא begins to narrow that dispute, a discussion that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Is a worshipped attached item forbidden for the Temple?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether something attached to the ground that was worshipped becomes unfit for גבוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is a worshipped item that is attached to the ground forbidden for Temple use, or is it not forbidden for Temple use?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question. Something attached to the ground that was worshipped is permitted for ordinary people, so is it also permitted for the בית המקדש?
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know that מחובר does not become forbidden for an ordinary person through worship. But an animal that was worshipped is unfit as a קרבן, so Temple use may have a stricter standard. The question is whether that stricter Temple standard also covers attached things.

keyTerms.meaning: something that was worshipped as an idol
attached to the ground
literally 'the Most High'; means use for the בית המקדש

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two kinds of use. For an ordinary person, the rule that מחובר is not forbidden is already settled. The question here is only about using it for the בית המקדש.

phrases.english: Is there a disqualification of a worshipped attached item for the Most High,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ אֵין נֶעֱבָד בִּמְחוּבָּר אֵצֶל גָּבוֹהַּ?
phrases.english: or is there no disqualification of a worshipped attached item for the Most High?

steps.triggerLanguage: יֵשׁ נֶעֱבָד בִּמְחוּבָּר אֵצֶל גָּבוֹהַּ אוֹ אֵין
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether נעבד במחובר is disqualified for Temple use, even though it is permitted for an ordinary person.

steps.title: Follow-up question about items used to prepare offerings
steps.stepSummary: If attached worshipped items are forbidden for the Temple, does this also apply to מכשירי קרבן?
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say that a worshipped attached item is forbidden for Temple use, are the things that help bring an offering treated like the offering itself, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second question that only matters if the first question is answered strictly. It asks whether the rule covers only the קרבן itself, or also the things used to bring it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal that was worshipped clearly cannot be a קרבן. But the מזבח is not itself an offering; it only helps bring one. So even if Temple use is stricter, the stricter rule might apply only to the offering itself.

keyTerms.meaning: 'if you say'; introduces a follow-up question that builds on one answer to the first question
items that help bring an offering, such as the מזבח
they are similar to

phrases.english: If you say
that a worshipped attached item is disqualified for the Most High,

phrases.aramaic: מַכְשִׁירֵי קׇרְבָּן כְּקׇרְבָּן דָּמוּ אוֹ לָא?
phrases.english: are the things that prepare an offering like the offering itself, or not?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם תִּמְצֵי לוֹמַר יֵשׁ נֶעֱבָד בִּמְחוּבָּר אֵצֶל גָּבוֹהַּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second-level question that depends on the strict answer to step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the Temple disqualification of נעבד extends to מכשירי קרבן.

steps.title: רבא proves the stricter answer from a prostitute's payment
steps.stepSummary: רבא argues with a קל וחומר: אתנן is forbidden for the Temple even when attached, so נעבד, which is stricter, should be forbidden too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: here is a קל וחומר. A prostitute's payment is permitted to an ordinary person even when it is detached, yet it is forbidden for the Temple even when it is attached. We know this because it says, 'Do not bring a prostitute's payment or the price of a dog,' and that verse makes no difference between detached and attached. A worshipped item is forbidden to an ordinary person when it is detached. Surely, then, it is forbidden for the Temple when it is attached!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא tries to answer with a קל וחומר. He compares נעבד to אתנן. Per רש״י, his answer covers the second question too: the פסוק says 'בית ה׳', which includes even building the בית המקדש, so even מכשירי קרבן are forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אתנן is the more lenient item, because an ordinary person may use it, yet the Temple rejects it even when it is attached. נעבד is the stricter item, because when detached it is forbidden even to an ordinary person. So רבא reasons that the Temple should certainly reject an attached נעבד.

keyTerms.meaning: a logical argument that moves from a lighter case to a stricter one
payment given to a prostitute
detached from the ground
an ordinary person, meaning non-Temple use
'is it not logical?'; the closing formula of a קל וחומר

phrases.english: Rava said: this follows from an a fortiori argument:
If a prostitute's payment, which is permitted to an ordinary person when detached,
is forbidden for the Most High when attached,

phrases.aramaic: דִּכְתִיב: ״לֹא תָבִיא אֶתְנַן זוֹנָה וּמְחִיר כֶּלֶב״,
phrases.english: as it is written: "You shall not bring the payment to a prostitute or the price of a dog",

phrases.aramaic: לָא שְׁנָא תָּלוּשׁ וְלָא שְׁנָא בִּמְחוּבָּר,
phrases.english: there is no difference between detached and attached,
then a worshipped item, which is forbidden to an ordinary person when detached,
is it not logical that it is forbidden for the Most High when attached?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attempts to resolve the question in step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: נעבד במחובר is forbidden for גבוה, derived through a קל וחומר from אתנן.
steps.raayaObject: That נעבד במחובר is disqualified for the Temple.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The verse 'לא תביא אתנן זונה' (דברים 23:19), which includes attached אתנן.

steps.title: רב הונא reverses רבא's argument
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע shows that the קל וחומר can be flipped: an attached נעבד is permitted for the Temple, so attached אתנן should be permitted too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא, son of רב יהושע, said to רבא: you could reverse it. A worshipped item is forbidden to an ordinary person when it is detached, yet it is permitted for the Temple when it is attached. We know this because it says 'their gods upon the mountains,' which means the mountains themselves are not their gods, and that rule makes no difference between ordinary use and Temple use. A prostitute's payment is permitted to an ordinary person when it is detached. Surely, then, it is permitted for the Temple when it is attached!
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא challenges רבא by building the opposite קל וחומר. He starts from נעבד and reaches a lenient conclusion about אתנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads 'אלהיהם על ההרים' as teaching that an attached item never becomes forbidden through worship, for anyone, including the Temple. Since נעבד is the stricter item and is still permitted when attached, the more lenient אתנן should also be permitted when attached. Because the argument works equally well in both directions, רבא's proof is weakened.

keyTerms.meaning: 'or reverse it'; turning a קל וחומר around to prove the opposite
'their gods upon the mountains'; the source that attached things do not become forbidden
there is no difference

steps.whatToRemember: A קל וחומר only works if we know which case is stricter. Here, each side can build the argument in its own direction. רבא answers this in step 6: when reasoning can go either way, we choose the strict direction.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ לְרָבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, said to Rava:
Or reverse it:

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה נֶעֱבָד שֶׁאָסוּר בְּתָלוּשׁ אֵצֶל הֶדְיוֹט —
phrases.english: If a worshipped item, which is forbidden to an ordinary person when detached,
is permitted for the Most High when attached,
as it is stated: "Their gods, upon the mountains"
and not that the mountains are their gods,

phrases.aramaic: לָא שְׁנָא לְהֶדְיוֹט וְלָא שְׁנָא לְגָבוֹהַּ;
phrases.english: with no difference between an ordinary person and the Most High;
then a prostitute's payment, which is permitted to an ordinary person when detached,
is it not logical that it is permitted for the Most High when attached?
phrases.notes: He is turning רבא's argument around, so now attached אתנן comes out permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ לְרָבָא: אוֹ חִילּוּף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's קל וחומר by reversing its direction.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's קל וחומר from אתנן to נעבד.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The starting point can be flipped. Since 'אלהיהם על ההרים' permits attached נעבד for everyone, including גבוה, a reverse קל וחומר would permit attached אתנן for גבוה, which contradicts the verse רבא relied on.

steps.title: The verse about the House of God is needed for something else
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע blocks a possible reply: 'בית ה׳ אלהיך' cannot be the source for forbidding attached אתנן, because the פסוק is needed for a different teaching (the פרה אדומה, or the hammered plates).
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say attached אתנן is forbidden because the פסוק says 'the House of the Lord your God,' that phrase is needed for what a ברייתא teaches: 'the House of the Lord your God' leaves out the פרה אדומה, which is not brought into the Temple. These are the words of רבי אליעזר. The חכמים say it comes to include hammered gold plates.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע is protecting his flipped קל וחומר. He shows that the פסוק 'בית ה׳ אלהיך' cannot be used to prove attached אתנן is forbidden, because that phrase already teaches something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might say attached אתנן is forbidden simply because of a פסוק, not because of logic. רב הונא answers that this phrase is already 'used up' by a ברייתא: רבי אליעזר learns from it that the פרה אדומה is not affected by אתנן, and the חכמים learn that even decorative plates hung in the מקדש are included. So the flipped קל וחומר still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The House of the Lord your God', the words in the פסוק forbidding אתנן
It is needed for, meaning this פסוק is already used for a different teaching
The פרה אדומה (red heifer), which is burned outside the מקדש
Thin hammered plates of gold, used as covering or decoration

phrases.english: And if you say it is forbidden because of 'the House of the Lord your God'
phrases.notes: דברים 23:19. He means: maybe this פסוק forbids attached אתנן anyway.

phrases.english: that phrase is needed for what was taught in a ברייתא:
'The House of the Lord your God' leaves out the cow
phrases.notes: The cow here is the פרה אדומה. It is not disqualified by being אתנן.

phrases.english: which does not come into the House,
these are the words of Rabbi Eliezer.
And the Sages say: it comes to include the hammered plates.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי מִשּׁוּם ״בֵּית ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ״ מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע's challenge by closing off a possible escape from his flipped קל וחומר.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using the פסוק 'בית ה׳ אלהיך' as an independent source to forbid attached אתנן.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק is already needed for another teaching (the פרה אדומה according to רבי אליעזר, the hammered plates according to the חכמים).

steps.title: רבא: when logic can go either way, we choose the strict side
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that his קל וחומר leads to a stringency and the flipped one leads to a leniency, and when both are possible we reason toward the stringency.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: I am reasoning toward the strict side, and you are reasoning toward the lenient side. When we can go either way, we reason toward the strict side.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends his original קל וחומר. He admits the logic can be flipped, but says that in such a case we follow the strict direction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא does not deny that רב הונא's flipped argument works logically. Instead he adds a rule for choosing between two opposite arguments: the strict one wins. So attached נעבד stays forbidden for the מקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: Toward the strict side
Toward the lenient side
We reason or argue (here: which direction we build the argument)

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is רבא answering רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע.

phrases.english: I am reasoning toward stringency,
and you are reasoning toward leniency —
when it can go to leniency or stringency, we reason toward stringency.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֲנָא קָאָמֵינָא לְחוּמְרָא, וְאַתְּ אָמְרַתְּ לְקוּלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבא answers the flipped קל וחומר of steps 4 and 5.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a general rule about how to choose between two opposite קל וחומר arguments, and that rule is tested right away.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adds a rule for choosing between two possible directions of reasoning
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the קל וחומר can be flipped, maybe attached נעבד and אתנן are both permitted.
steps.terutzMaskana: When reasoning can go either way, we go with the strict direction, so attached נעבד is forbidden.

steps.title: רב פפא: רבי עקיבא reasoned toward leniency
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא challenges רבא's rule using the case of הזאה for the קרבן פסח, where רבי עקיבא reasons toward the lenient side against רבי אליעזר's strict reasoning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to רבא: Is it true that whenever we could go strict or lenient, we never reason toward the lenient side? But what about sprinkling for the פסח, where רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא argue? רבי אליעזר reasons strictly and makes the man obligated, while רבי עקיבא reasons leniently and exempts him. So רבי עקיבא does reason toward the lenient side!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא attacks רבא's rule. He brings a known argument where a great תנא, רבי עקיבא, chose the lenient direction of reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said we always reason toward the strict side. רב פפא points to the argument about הזאה on שבת: רבי אליעזר's reasoning obligates the person in the פסח, while רבי עקיבא's reversed reasoning exempts him. If רבי עקיבא can reason leniently, רבא's rule is not absolute.

keyTerms.meaning: Sprinkling the water of the פרה אדומה to purify someone who became impure from a dead body
The קרבן פסח (Passover offering)
Makes obligated
Exempts

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'lenient' means exempting the person from bringing the פסח, and 'strict' means obligating him, even though the strict view lets him sprinkle on שבת.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Rava:
And anywhere there is a leniency and a stringency,
do we never reason toward leniency?
But what about the sprinkling for the Pesach,
phrases.notes: The question is whether we sprinkle on שבת a person impure from a dead body, so he can bring the פסח.

phrases.english: where Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Akiva disagree,
for Rabbi Eliezer holds toward stringency
and makes the man obligated,
and Rabbi Akiva holds toward leniency and exempts him,
so Rabbi Akiva does reason toward leniency!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְרָבָא: וְכֹל הֵיכָא דְּאִיכָּא קוּלָּא וְחוּמְרָא, לְקוּלָּא לָא פָּרְכִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule רבא just gave in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's rule that between a strict and lenient קל וחומר we always choose the strict one.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי עקיבא, in the הזאה argument, reverses רבי אליעזר's strict reasoning to reach a lenient result, so lenient reasoning is used.

steps.title: The משנה where רבי עקיבא reverses the argument
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה showing רבי עקיבא's reversed קל וחומר: if הזאה, only a שבות, does not override שבת, then שחיטה, which is a Torah prohibition, surely does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: רבי עקיבא answered, 'Or reverse it: if sprinkling, which is forbidden only by the Rabbis, does not override שבת, then slaughtering, which is forbidden by the Torah, surely does not!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רב פפא's challenge by quoting the actual משנה. It shows רבי עקיבא's words where he flips the argument toward the lenient side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא turns the comparison around: the lighter prohibition (הזאה, a rabbinic שבות) does not override שבת, so the heavier one (שחיטה, a Torah prohibition) certainly should not. This is a clear case of reasoning toward leniency, which seems to contradict רבא's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Or reverse it, meaning flip the argument the other way
A rabbinic prohibition on שבת
Overrides, pushes aside
Slaughtering an animal
From the Torah

steps.whatToRemember: רבא says that when a קל וחומר can go either way, we go strict. רב פפא challenges this, because רבי עקיבא flipped רבי אליעזר's argument to reach a lenient result.

phrases.english: As we learned in a Mishnah: Rabbi Akiva replied:
phrases.notes: He is replying to רבי אליעזר's argument: if שחיטה overrides שבת for the פסח, surely the lighter הזאה does too.

phrases.english: Or reverse it,
and if sprinkling, which is forbidden only as a rabbinic prohibition —
does not override Shabbat,
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁחִיטָה שֶׁהִיא דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא — לֹא כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן?
phrases.english: then slaughtering, which is forbidden by the Torah — all the more so should it not!

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן, הֵשִׁיב רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: אוֹ חִילּוּף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the משנה that supports רב פפא's challenge in step 7.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי עקיבא reasons toward leniency, against רבא's rule.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in פסחים 65b with רבי עקיבא's reply 'או חילוף'.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא Was Only Reminding רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers רב פפא's challenge: in the הזאה case, רבי עקיבא was not really deriving a lenient rule. רבי אליעזר had taught it to him and forgotten it, so רבי עקיבא was helping him remember.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, רבי אליעזר had taught it to him, but he forgot his learning, and רבי עקיבא came to remind him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא's rule that we reason toward the stringency. It explains that the case of רבי עקיבא is not a real counter-example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא argued that רבי עקיבא chose the lenient קל וחומר over the strict one. The גמרא answers that רבי עקיבא's argument was really a reminder of a tradition he had received from רבי אליעזר. So it was never a free choice between two lines of reasoning, and רבא's rule still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: He taught it to him
His learning became 'heavy' for him, meaning he forgot it
To remind him

phrases.english: There, Rabbi Eliezer taught it to him,
phrases.notes: 'There' means the הזאה case from the משנה quoted in step 8.

phrases.english: but his learning became heavy for him (he forgot it),
and Rabbi Akiva came to remind him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's challenge (steps 7-8) against רבא's rule
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the source: the קל וחומר was a memory aid, not real reasoning
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי עקיבא chose a lenient קל וחומר over a strict one, which goes against רבא's rule
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי עקיבא was reminding רבי אליעזר of a received tradition, so the case does not go against רבא's rule

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's Own Words Prove He Was Quoting a Tradition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports its answer with רבי עקיבא's words: 'Do not deny me; this is what I received from you: הזאה is a שבות and does not override שבת.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what he said to him: 'My teacher, do not make me deny it at the time of the ruling. This is what I received from you: הזאה is a שבות and does not override שבת.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings proof for its answer from רבי עקיבא's own words to רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא openly says he received this rule from רבי אליעזר. That shows his קל וחומר was meant to jog his teacher's memory, not to invent a lenient rule. This backs up the answer in step 9.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not make me deny it, or do not deny me
At the time of judgment, meaning while the ruling is being decided
I received this as a tradition from you

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's rule holds: when a קל וחומר can be built in two directions, we go toward the stringency. רבי עקיבא's lenient argument was really a reminder of a tradition.

phrases.english: And this is what he said to him:
phrases.notes: רבי עקיבא is speaking to his teacher, רבי אליעזר.

phrases.english: My teacher, do not deny me at the time of judgment,
this is what I received from you:

phrases.english: sprinkling is a rabbinic prohibition, and it does not override Shabbat.

steps.title: Can Worshipped Wheat Be Used for Meal Offerings?
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא asks: if someone bowed down to standing wheat, may that wheat be used for מנחות? Does a change in the form of a נעבד remove its ban or not?
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא asked: if someone bows down to a standing stalk of wheat, may it be used for מנחות? Does a change in form help for a worshipped object, or doesn't it?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question opens. רמי בר חמא asks whether worshipped wheat that later changes form, for example by being ground into flour, may be brought as a מנחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Standing wheat that was bowed down to becomes a נעבד, which is not allowed on the מזבח. But a מנחה is brought as flour, not as standing stalks. The question is whether that change in form makes it a new thing that is no longer forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: One who bows down in worship
Standing grain of wheat, still attached to the ground
Meal offerings brought from flour
A change in form

phrases.english: Rami bar Chama asked:
one who bows down to a standing stalk of wheat,
what is the law about using it for meal offerings?
Does a change in form count for a worshipped object,
phrases.notes: The wheat was worshipped as a stalk, but a מנחה is made from flour. That is the 'change.'

phrases.english: or does a change in form not count for a worshipped object?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the קל וחומר discussion ends
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a change in form removes the ban on a נעבד for use on the מזבח

steps.title: מר זוטרא Tries to Answer from Offspring of Forbidden Animals
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא brings a משנה: the offspring of anything forbidden for the מזבח are permitted, while a ברייתא says רבי אליעזר forbids them.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא son of רב נחמן said: Come and hear. All things forbidden for the מזבח have offspring that are permitted. And a ברייתא taught about it: רבי אליעזר forbids them.
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא offers a possible answer to רמי בר חמא's question from a known משנה and the ברייתא taught about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An offspring is like a new form that came from a forbidden animal. The first opinion permits the offspring and רבי אליעזר forbids it. That seems to be the same debate as whether a change in form removes the ban, so the question would depend on this dispute.

keyTerms.meaning: Things forbidden to be offered on the altar
Their offspring
And it was taught about it, introducing a ברייתא on the משנה

phrases.english: Mar Zutra, son of Rav Nachman, said:

steps.title: The Offspring Dispute Is Limited to a Specific Case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: רב נחמן quoted רבה בר אבוה that the dispute is only about animals that were used for bestiality and became pregnant afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it said about this: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה, the dispute is where the animals were used for bestiality and only later became pregnant.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to question מר זוטרא's proof by pointing out that the offspring dispute applies only to a narrow case. The explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מר זוטרא used the offspring dispute as a general debate about change in form. Now the גמרא notes that the argument is about one specific setup: the animal became forbidden first and became pregnant afterward. Because the dispute is this narrow, it may not answer רמי בר חמא's question, and the גמרא goes on to explain why.

keyTerms.meaning: But wasn't it stated about this? This introduces a limiting statement
The dispute
They were used for bestiality, which makes an animal forbidden for the מזבח
They became pregnant

phrases.english: But wasn't it stated about this,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said in the name of Rabba bar Avuh:
the dispute is where they were used for bestiality
and only afterward became pregnant,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts to weaken מר זוטרא's proof by narrowing the dispute he relied on
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: מר זוטרא's proof from the offspring dispute
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The dispute is limited to a specific case (bestiality first, pregnancy later), so it may not be a general debate about change in form
